newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal approves 97 budget, projected deficit down.
newsitem.headline: Senegal approves 97 budget, projected deficit down.

text.p: Senegal's parliament has approved a 1997 budget with a slightly lower deficit than in 1996, thanks in part to an increase in Value Added Tax from 10 to 20 percent on imported goods.
Officials said the aim of the budget, which was approved late on Friday (Eds correct), was to cut inflation further and boost growth.
The 1997 budget projects revenue of 438 billion CFA francs, 9.48 percent up on 1996. The projected deficit drops from 54.9 billion CFA to 52 billion CFA.
Officials said the state would borrow on the national and international markets and from development partners to make up the deficit.
Senegal and other Francophone nations in West and Central Africa devalued their common CFA franc currency by 50 percent in 1994 as part of efforts to turn round their flagging economies.

The budget draft targets Gross Domestic Product growth of five percent in 1997 with inflation of under two percent. GDP growth was 4.5 percent in 1995, inflation was eight percent. The 1996 GDP target is five percent, inflation three percent.
Senegal's foreign debt stands at 1,700 billion CFA.
